articles.title: Hawai'i vs North Dakota State: A 13-7 Lead Slips Away in the Fourth, 21-13
articles.matchup: Final: North Dakota State Bison (8-2) 21, Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors (3-7) 13, Sat., Nov. 14, Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex, Honolulu. Next: at Nevada, Sat., Nov. 21, 10:30 PM ET, Mackay Stadium, Reno
articles.text:
Warrior fans, this one stings. North Dakota State 21, Hawai'i 13 on Saturday night at the Ching Complex, and we're 3-7. We led 13-7 going into the fourth quarter with 15,014 of us making all the noise we could. We just couldn't close it.

The first half was a slog. An early interception at our 15 set them up for a quick touchdown, and it was 7-0. But right before the break, DeVon Rice took a handoff 15 yards for a touchdown with 4 seconds left, and Sean Olvera-Harle tied it with the kick. That's a Rainbow Warrior answer.

Then Olvera-Harle went to work. He drilled a 28-yard field goal midway through the third and a 33-yarder late in the quarter. 13-7, us. Our defense was flying around, too. Jamih Otis made seven tackles with three for loss, and Kona Moore had seven with two for loss. North Dakota State managed 86 rushing yards and 183 yards of offense all night.

The fourth quarter is what hurts. They put together a 16-play drive that ate more than eight minutes and scored to go up 14-13. Then on our next possession, a throw got jumped and returned 49 yards for a touchdown. In about two minutes, a lead turned into an eight-point hole.

Micah Alejado battled. He completed 31 of 47 throws for 231 yards. Kainoa Carvalho caught seven for 63, Titan Lacaden had six, and Tama Uiliata had five catches and 34 punt return yards. We went for it on fourth down twice late and came up short both times.

Gehrig Heil punted five times, with four inside the 20, and pinned them deep almost every time. I'm proud of how hard these guys played. We just needed one more stop.

Next up: Hawai'i heads to Reno to face Nevada at Mackay Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 21, 10:30 PM ET. Imua, Warriors.

articles.title: North Dakota State vs Hawai'i: Ray James Jr. Takes One Back as the Bison Rally, 21-13
articles.byline: Ingeborg 'Inga' Halvorsen, The North Dakota State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: North Dakota State Bison (8-2) 21, Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors (3-7) 13, Sat., Nov. 14, Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex, Honolulu. Next: vs Northern Illinois, Sat., Nov. 21, 4:00 PM ET, Fargodome, Fargo
articles.text:
Go Bison! North Dakota State 21, Hawai'i 13 on Saturday night at the Ching Complex in Honolulu, and we are 8-2 and 5-2 in the Mountain West. Somewhere back in Fargo it was well past bedtime, and I promise you every one of us was still awake for the fourth quarter.

It started like we drew it up. Logan Larson intercepted Micah Alejado on their second possession and set us up at their 11. Two plays later, Nathan Hayes hit Mekhi Collins for a 7-yard touchdown. 7-0 after one.

Then it got sticky. Our offense couldn't get rolling, they scored with 4 seconds left before the half, and their kicker hit two field goals in the third quarter. We went into the fourth down 13-7, and I had my rally cap on backward and inside out.

That's when this team did what it always does. We took the ball at our own 23 and went 77 yards in 16 plays, eating 8:37 off the clock. Pure Bison football. DJ Scott finished it with a 1-yard plunge and Drew Klein made the kick. 14-13, us, with 8:34 left.

Less than two minutes later, Ray James Jr. jumped a throw and ran it back 49 yards for a touchdown. 21-13. The Ching Complex went quiet, and I nearly fell off my couch. James also made 10 solo tackles. What a night.

The defense held Hawai'i to 31 rushing yards on 26 carries and stopped them on fourth down twice in the final minutes. Matthew Stenbroten had 1.5 sacks and 3.5 tackles for loss. Keenan Wilson had two sacks. Aaron Bickerton averaged 46 yards on seven punts and kept flipping the field all night. We only gained 183 yards and still won by eight. That's how you win in November.

Next up: the Bison come home to the Fargodome to host Northern Illinois, Saturday, Nov. 21, 4 PM ET. Bring the noise, Bison Nation.

articles.title: Colorado State vs Washington State: A Long Night in Pullman Ends 73-7
articles.byline: Ansel Rimrock, The Colorado State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Washington State Cougars (2-8) 73, Colorado State Rams (3-7) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Martin Stadium, Pullman. Next: at Fresno State, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET, Valley Children's Stadium, Fresno
articles.text:
Rams fans, I drove a long way to Pullman, and I'll drive a long way home. Washington State 73, Colorado State 7 on Saturday night at Martin Stadium. We're 3-7 and 1-5 in the Pac-12, and there is no sugarcoating this one. We got flattened by a train in crimson.

The numbers hurt to type. They ran for 535 yards and nine touchdowns, both school records for them. One of their backs went 98 yards from his own 2. Their quarterback missed one throw all night. We were down 35-0 before we scored.

When we did score, it was a good one. With 38 seconds left in the half, RJ Vick plunged in from a yard out and Kali Nguma added the kick. Vick also caught two balls for 47 yards. Hauss Hejny threw for 199 yards, completing 14 of 24, and Tommy Maher caught four for 76 yards. Durell Robinson had a 35-yard catch. There were a few moments where you could see what this offense wants to be.

But we lost a fumble late in the first quarter, threw an interception in the third, and went 0 for 3 on fourth down. We converted 3 of 11 third downs. You can't win like that anywhere, and you really can't win like that in Pullman.

I want to give credit to the guys who never stopped hitting. Oumar Diomande made eight tackles. Tre'Shawn Moore had seven, and Jaylen King and D'Angelo Hagans Jr. had six apiece. Mel Brown returned four kickoffs for 70 yards. Nathan Sutcliffe punted five times.

We're still winless on the road this year, and that has to change. Lift your heads, Rams. Nobody remembers a night like this if the next one is better.

Next up: Colorado State travels to Fresno to face Fresno State at Valley Children's Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 PM ET. Let's go, Rams.

articles.title: Washington State vs Colorado State: Kirby Vorhees Goes 98 Yards in a Record 73-7 Romp
articles.byline: Hank Palouse, The Washington State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Washington State Cougars (2-8) 73, Colorado State Rams (3-7) 7, Sat., Nov. 14, Martin Stadium, Pullman. Next: at Texas State, Sat., Nov. 21, 6:00 PM ET, UFCU Stadium, San Marcos
articles.text:
Go Cougs, and I mean GO. Washington State 73, Colorado State 7 on Saturday night at Martin Stadium in Pullman. Six straight losses, gone. We're 2-8, 1-5 in the Pac-12, and I don't care what the record says this morning. That was the most fun I've had on the Palouse in a long, long time.

Kirby Vorhees, come on down. Twelve carries. 197 yards. Four touchdowns. The yards and the touchdowns are both career highs. He scored from 3 yards to open it, and then with 55 seconds left in the first quarter, he took a first-down handoff from our own 2 and ran 98 yards. Ninety-eight! It's a Pac-12 record and the longest touchdown run in the country this season. I spilled my coffee and didn't even notice.

Owen Eshelman was nearly perfect. He completed 13 of 14 throws for 135 yards, hit Branden Ganashamoorthy for a 30-yard touchdown three plays into the third quarter, and ran for three more scores from 4, 9 and 1 yards. Maxwell Woods ran for 108 yards and a 2-yard score. Then Julian Dugger came in and took off for 60 yards for the final touchdown.

Count them up. Nine rushing touchdowns, a school record. 535 rushing yards, also a school record, beating the 424 we put up against Idaho in 1975. We had 300 on the ground by halftime and led 38-7 after Jack Stevens kicked a 33-yard field goal on the final play of the half. Stevens went 9 for 9 on extra points.

The defense deserves love, too. Matyus McLain recovered a fumble late in the first quarter, and Jaylen Thomas intercepted a throw in the third and returned three punts for 43 yards. Keith Brown made nine tackles. Jalil Tucker had a sack. Colorado State went 0 for 3 on fourth down and finished with 61 rushing yards.

Seventy-three points. Let the whole Palouse hear it, Cougs. Next up: Washington State heads to San Marcos to face Texas State at UFCU Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 21, 6 PM ET.

articles.title: Arizona vs Utah: Fifita Throws for 356, but the Wildcats Fall 40-39 in a Midnight Thriller
articles.matchup: Final: Utah Utes (10-0) 40, Arizona Wildcats (7-3) 39, Sat., Nov. 14, Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson. Next: at Kansas State, Sat., Nov. 21, 7:00 PM ET, Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Manhattan
articles.text:
Wildcat fans, I have been staring at the ceiling for an hour. Utah 40, Arizona 39 at Casino Del Sol Stadium, and we're 7-3. It was the highest-ranked opponent to play in Tucson since Oregon in 2007, and we were 38 seconds away from beating them.

We came out swinging. Quincy Craig plunged in from a yard in the first quarter. Kedrick Reescano scored from 5 in the second. It was 14-3, and 48,858 people in Tucson were losing their minds. Utah answered with two quarterback runs to lead 17-14 at the half.

Then Mays Pese recovered a fumble at their 18 on the first snap of the third quarter, and Noah Fifita hit Isaiah Mizell for a 6-yard touchdown. 21-17, us. Jay'Vion Cole intercepted a throw at our own 1 later in the quarter, and Fifita found Giovanni Richardson for a 19-yard score to make it 28-24.

Fifita was magnificent. He finished 27 of 43 for 356 yards and three touchdowns. Chris Hunter III caught six balls for 119 yards. Mizell had seven catches for 115 and two scores. Richardson had seven for 94.

The fourth quarter was a heavyweight fight. Drew Nicolson recovered a muffed punt at their 17, and Michael Salgado-Medina kicked a 47-yarder to make it 33-31. Then Fifita found Mizell from 10 yards with 3:13 left and ran in the two-point try himself. 39-33.

And 38 seconds later, Utah hit a 70-yard touchdown. We got one more chance near midfield, but the fourth-down throw was broken up with 1:56 left. Chase Kennedy made nine tackles and Tyrese Boss broke up two throws. Nobody on this team has anything to hang their heads about.

Seven and three, and still plenty to play for. Next up: the Wildcats head to Manhattan to face Kansas State at Bill Snyder Family Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 21, 7 PM ET. Bear Down!

The fourth quarter was a heavyweight fight. Drew Nicolson recovered a muffed punt at their 17, and Michael Salgado-Medina kicked a 47-yarder to make it 33-31. Then Fifita found Mizell from 10 yards with 3:13 left and ran in the two-point try himself. 39-33.

articles.title: Utah vs Arizona: Dampier to Whittemore for 70 Yards, Utes Survive 40-39 and Stay Perfect
articles.matchup: Final: Utah Utes (10-0) 40, Arizona Wildcats (7-3) 39, Sat., Nov. 14, Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson. Next: at TCU, Sat., Nov. 21, 9:00 PM ET, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth
articles.text:
Utes fans, I need a minute. Utah 40, Arizona 39 at Casino Del Sol Stadium in Tucson, in a game that ended early Sunday morning, and we are 10-0 and 7-0 in the Big 12. Sixteen straight wins across two seasons. My heart rate may never recover.

Remember, this team didn't even land in Tucson until just after noon on Saturday after Friday's FAA ground stop, and the game got pushed back three hours. Then we fell behind 14-3. No excuses, though. That's not how we do it in Salt Lake.

Devon Dampier dragged us back. He ran for scores from 14 and 18 yards in the second quarter, and we led 17-14 at the half. Braden Pegan even intercepted a heave on the final play of the half. Dampier fumbled on the first snap of the third and threw an interception at their 1 later in the quarter, but he also hit Byrd Ficklin for a 4-yard touchdown in between. He finished with 100 rushing yards and 204 through the air.

And Daniel Bray. Oh, Daniel Bray. Eighteen carries, 197 yards, a 62-yard burst, and an 8-yard touchdown that made it 33-28 early in the fourth. Dillon Curtis drilled field goals from 53 and 39. Orion Phillips averaged 56.3 yards a punt, with a long of 84. Let that sink in.

Then it got scary. A muffed punt set up an Arizona field goal, and their quarterback threw a 10-yard touchdown and ran in the two-point try to put them up 39-33 with 3:13 left. Thirty-eight seconds later, Dampier let it fly and Creed Whittemore ran it down for a 70-yard touchdown. Curtis made the kick. 40-39. I screamed loud enough to wake the whole block.

The defense still had to finish. On fourth down near midfield with less than two minutes left, Jackson Bennee broke up the throw. Ballgame. Rabbit Evans had seven tackles, and Elijah Davis and Trey Reynolds had six each.

Perfect in November. Next up, the Utes head to Fort Worth to face TCU at Amon G. Carter Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 21, 9 PM ET. Go Utes!

articles.title: UTEP vs Wyoming: Raymond Moore III Runs Wild, but the Miners Fall 27-15
articles.matchup: Final: Wyoming Cowboys (7-3) 27, UTEP Miners (1-9) 15, Sat., Nov. 14, Sun Bowl, El Paso. Next: at Air Force, Fri., Nov. 20, 8:00 PM ET, Falcon Stadium, USAF Academy
articles.text:
Miner fans, I'm going to start with the good, because there was good. Raymond Moore III took off on an 80-yard touchdown run about seven minutes into Saturday night's game at the Sun Bowl, and for a minute, El Paso was flying. Then the rest of the night happened. Wyoming 27, UTEP 15. We're 1-9.

Moore was the best player on the field for us. He ran 20 times for 164 yards and completed 11 of 19 throws. When he got loose, the whole stadium came to its feet. He's a gamer, and he keeps getting up.

But the first half got away. Wyoming went 93 yards for a touchdown to take a 7-6 lead, and then a bad snap got past our punter, Brady Braun, at our 21. One play later, it was 14-6. They added a touchdown run and a field goal before the half, and it was 24-6 at the break. Braun, for the record, still averaged 53 yards a punt. The man has a leg.

The defense kept fighting, and I want them to hear it. Kode Lowe forced a fumble that Leander Parrish recovered early in the second quarter. Jayden Wilson knocked another one loose late in the third, and Justin Content fell on it. Shakaun Bowser forced a third one in the fourth, and Parrish scooped it up again and returned it 11 yards. Garrett Hawkins made 10 tackles. Wilson had nine.

Carlos Arreola nailed a 55-yard field goal at the end of the third quarter, and Elijah McCoy powered in from a yard out to make it 24-15 with 12:00 left. We missed the two-point try, missed a field goal later, and came up short on a fourth down. Close, but not enough.

Eight straight losses is hard to type. But this team keeps showing up, and so will I.

Next up: the Miners travel to Colorado Springs to face Air Force at Falcon Stadium, Friday, Nov. 20, 8 PM ET. Keep swinging, Miners.

articles.title: Wyoming vs UTEP: Landon Sims Shines in His First Start as the Pokes Win 27-15
articles.matchup: Final: Wyoming Cowboys (7-3) 27, UTEP Miners (1-9) 15, Sat., Nov. 14, Sun Bowl, El Paso. Next: vs New Mexico, Fri., Nov. 20, 9:00 PM ET, War Memorial Stadium, Laramie
articles.text:
Ride 'em, Pokes! Wyoming 27, UTEP 15 on Saturday night at the Sun Bowl in El Paso, and we are 7-3 and 6-1 in the Mountain West. And after New Mexico lost 21-17 to UNLV earlier in the night, we're tied with the Lobos at the top of the league. I'm wearing my brown and gold to bed.

Landon Sims made his first career start and played like he'd been doing it for years. He finished 19 of 25 for 289 yards and a touchdown. Kyle Frendt caught four balls for 113 yards, and Samuel Harris did a little of everything with 66 rushing yards, 82 receiving yards and two scores.

We did fall behind first. Their quarterback broke an 80-yard touchdown run about seven minutes in, and it was 6-0. So we marched 93 yards, and our running back, Markell Holman, threw a 3-yard touchdown to Landon Pace. That's our first touchdown throw by a non-quarterback since Austin Conway threw one to Josh Allen back in 2016. Laramie remembers. 7-6, us.

Then UTEP's punter couldn't handle the snap, Jett Vincent fell on it at their 21, and Sims hit Harris for a 21-yard touchdown on the very next play. Harris added a 33-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, Erik Sandvik made a 30-yard field goal before the half, and it was 24-6.

I won't pretend the second half was clean. We lost three fumbles, and UTEP kicked a 55-yarder and scored on a 1-yard run to make it 24-15 early in the fourth. Sandvik settled it with a 41-yard field goal with 6:40 left. Then Jack Dunkley sacked their quarterback on fourth down to end their last real threat.

Ethan Stuhlsatz led the defense with 11 tackles and 1.5 tackles for loss, Gary Rutherford had eight, and Bart Edmiston averaged 46.3 yards a punt. Sandvik went 2 for 2 on field goals and 3 for 3 on extra points.

Now the big one. New Mexico comes to War Memorial Stadium in Laramie on Friday, Nov. 20, 9 PM ET, with first place on the table. Bundle up and get loud, Cowboy Joe is waiting.

articles.title: Utah State vs San Diego State: A Kicker's Throw Sinks the Aggies, 30-13
articles.byline: Hyrum Tolleson, The Utah State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: San Diego State Aztecs (5-5) 30, Utah State Aggies (4-6) 13, Sat., Nov. 14, Snapdragon Stadium, San Diego. Next: at Oregon State, Sat., Nov. 21, 10:30 PM ET, Reser Stadium, Corvallis
articles.text:
Aggie fans, I've got a sore throat and a heavy heart. San Diego State 30, Utah State 13 on Saturday night at Snapdragon Stadium. We're 4-6, and we are still looking for our first road win of the year.

The opening was weird but wonderful. McCae Hillstead carried it into the end zone from 2 yards and lost the ball as he got there, and Nehemiah Washington pounced on it for the touchdown. Washington gets the stat, Hillstead gets the effort, and we led 7-0 midway through the first. Kian Afrookhteh added the kick.

That was our last lead. The Aztecs kicked a field goal, scored late in the half to go up 10-7, and then pulled a fake field goal in the third quarter, with their kicker throwing a 20-yard touchdown to a linebacker. I've seen a lot of football in Logan. I'm still in shock. Down 17-7, and the offense never found its feet again.

Hillstead finished 17 of 34 for 139 yards. We ran for 61 yards on 29 carries. We were 3 of 14 on third down, and twice in the fourth quarter we went for it on fourth down and got sacked. That's a hard way to live.

I'll give our guys this: nobody quit. D'Angelo Mayes intercepted a throw early in the third quarter and returned it 29 yards, and he made nine tackles. Bobby Arnold had 10 tackles, and Brevin Hamblin had nine. Hillstead hit Anthony Garcia for a 5-yard touchdown with 1:10 left, and we didn't give the ball away once all night. Landon Rehkow punted eight times and kept us in the fight.

Garcia caught three balls for 36 yards. Noah White ran for 36 more and caught four. There are pieces here, and there's still football left.

Next up: the Aggies travel to Corvallis to face Oregon State at Reser Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 21, 10:30 PM ET. Let's go get that road win, Aggies.

articles.title: San Diego State vs Utah State: Cooper DiLeva Kicks Three and Throws One in a 30-13 Win
articles.byline: Kai Delgado-Sorensen, The San Diego State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: San Diego State Aztecs (5-5) 30, Utah State Aggies (4-6) 13, Sat., Nov. 14, Snapdragon Stadium, San Diego. Next: at Boise State, Sat., Nov. 21, 9:30 PM ET, Albertsons Stadium, Boise
articles.text:
Aztec fans, our kicker threw a touchdown. Let me say that again for the folks in the back at Snapdragon Stadium: our kicker threw a touchdown. San Diego State 30, Utah State 13 on Saturday night, and we're 5-5 with a 4-2 conference mark.

It did not begin pretty. Utah State scored first on a fumble that their own guy fell on in the end zone, and it was 7-0 midway through the first quarter. Cooper DiLeva got us on the board with a 31-yard field goal, and late in the half Lucky Sutton punched in a 4-yard run. 10-7 at the break.

Then came the play I'll be telling my grandkids about. Midway through the third quarter, DiLeva set up for what looked like a 38-yard try. The holder flicked the ball behind his back to DiLeva, he rolled right, and he floated it to linebacker Kai Wallin, who was so wide open he could have stopped for a fish taco. Twenty yards, touchdown, 17-7. A linebacker scoring on a throw from a kicker. That's Aztec football, baby.

DiLeva wasn't done. He hit from 42 yards before the third quarter ended and from 34 early in the fourth. Three field goals, one touchdown throw, three extra points. Twelve points from one guy. Somebody get that man a parking spot.

The ground game carried the rest. Javion Kinnard ran 19 times for 113 yards and added 47 yards on punt returns. Sutton had 96 yards on 21 carries and sealed it with a 2-yard score with 2:12 left. Nathan Acevedo caught eight balls for 92 yards. Stone Saunders threw one interception, but we outgained them 410 to 200.

And the defense was nasty. Utah State managed 61 rushing yards. Sione Hala had a sack and two tackles for loss, and his sack ended a fourth-down try in our territory. Tano Letuli made eight tackles. Three of the last four are wins for us.

Big one next. The Aztecs head to Boise to face Boise State at Albertsons Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 21, 9:30 PM ET. Let's go steal one on the blue turf, fellas.

articles.title: Oklahoma State vs Texas Tech: A 17-Point Comeback Fades in the Stillwater Rain, 52-27
articles.byline: Dusty Lockridge, The Oklahoma State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Tech Red Raiders (9-1) 52, Oklahoma State Cowboys (6-4) 27, Sat., Nov. 14, Boone Pickens Stadium, Stillwater. Next: at Arizona State, Sat., Nov. 21, 10:15 PM ET, Mountain America Stadium, Tempe
articles.text:
Cowboy fans, I stayed until the very end, soaked through and stubborn. Texas Tech 52, Oklahoma State 27, at Boone Pickens Stadium on a cold, rainy Saturday night that turned into Sunday. We're 6-4, and this one hurt from the opening kick.

Literally from the opening kick. Their return man went 97 yards for a touchdown 14 seconds in, and by the end of the first quarter it was 21-0. Drew Mestemaker got intercepted at our 29 in that stretch, too. I've seen better openings at a church potluck.

But this team doesn't quit, and I love them for it. Sam Keltner opened our scoring with a 40-yard field goal. Isaiah Chisom forced a fumble, Jerry Lawson fell on it at their 13, and Mestemaker ran it in himself from 13 yards on the next snap. Then he found Morgan McPhaul for an 18-yard touchdown with 3:55 left in the half, and it was 21-17. Boone Pickens was rocking. We had 17 straight points.

It lasted 17 seconds. Their quarterback scrambled and found a receiver for 80 yards. Keltner hit a 24-yard field goal before the break to make it 28-20, but the third quarter was where it got away. We went for it on fourth down twice and came up empty both times, and they scored early to go up 35-20.

Mestemaker threw for 277 yards before he came out late. He's still the guy who'd thrown for 300 yards in eight straight games, and he'll be fine. Caleb Hawkins ran for 91 yards and caught eight balls. Terrence Lewis and Justin Bowick each had 78 receiving yards. Evan Jackson made 10 solo tackles. Freshman Broderick Vehrs came in and led a drive that William Mason finished with a 10-yard run in the last minute.

Six and four is not where we wanted to be in mid-November. But we beat Kansas State 66-28 a week ago, and this group can still finish strong. Hold your heads high, boys.

Next up: the Cowboys fly to Tempe to face Arizona State at Mountain America Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 21, 10:15 PM ET. Go Pokes!

articles.title: Texas Tech vs Oklahoma State: Simmons Takes the Opening Kick 97 Yards in a 52-27 Rout
articles.byline: Bodie Ratliff, The Texas Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Texas Tech Red Raiders (9-1) 52, Oklahoma State Cowboys (6-4) 27, Sat., Nov. 14, Boone Pickens Stadium, Stillwater. Next: at Baylor, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, McLane Stadium, Waco
articles.text:
Raider Power, everybody. Texas Tech 52, Oklahoma State 27, late Saturday night into Sunday morning at Boone Pickens Stadium in Stillwater, and we are 9-1. Cold, rainy, and almost midnight back home in Lubbock, and I would not trade one minute of it.

It took 14 seconds. Malcolm Simmons fielded the opening kickoff and went 97 yards untouched to the end zone, and you could hear 52,168 people go silent. Then J'Koby Williams ripped off a 34-yard touchdown run less than three minutes later. Thomas Castellanos hit Terrance Carter Jr. from 8 yards before the first quarter ended, and it was 21-0. Guns up, Stillwater.

I'll be honest, the Cowboys made me sweat in the second quarter. Castellanos fumbled at our 14, they ran off 17 straight points, and it was 21-17. But Castellanos answered 17 seconds later by escaping the rush and finding Micah Hudson for an 80-yard touchdown. That throw was the night. We went into the half up 28-20.

The second half belonged to us. Castellanos hit Simmons for a 45-yard score early in the third quarter, then found Kenny Johnson from 30 yards on the first play of the fourth. He finished 12 of 23 for 263 yards and four touchdowns and then got to sit for most of the last quarter. Simmons had a 97-yard return and a 45-yard catch. Williams ran 19 times for 124 yards. Stone Harrington drilled a 54-yard field goal, and Cameron Dickey punched in a 2-yard run to make it 52-20.

And the defense? It intercepted Drew Mestemaker twice, John Curry in the first quarter and Ben Roberts in the fourth. Roberts also made 13 tackles. The Cowboys went for it on fourth down four times and came away with one first down. Austin Romaine had eight stops.

Nine and one. That's how the reigning Big 12 champs carry themselves in November.

Next up: the Red Raiders head to Waco to face Baylor at McLane Stadium, Saturday, Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET. Wreck 'Em, Tech!

articles.title: Pittsburgh vs Florida State: Panthers Defense Battles, Falls 16-10 at Home
articles.matchup: Final: Florida State Seminoles (5-5) 16, Pittsburgh Panthers (6-4) 10, Fri., Nov. 13, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: at Louisville, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville
articles.text:
Yinz, I'm not gonna sugarcoat it. Florida State 16, Pittsburgh 10 on Friday night at Acrisure Stadium, and the Panthers are 6-4. There were 45,734 of us bundled up on the North Shore, and we deserved a happier walk home across the river.

The defense showed up, I'll give 'em that. Florida State managed 260 yards, ran for just 97 on 33 carries and converted 3 of 13 third downs. Cruce Brookins was everywhere with 10 tackles. Braylan Lovelace forced a fumble and had a tackle and a half for loss. Early in the fourth, Alex Sanford Jr. knocked the ball loose from Ashton Daniels and Shawn Lee Jr. fell on it at our 6 to keep it a 13-10 game.

Our lone touchdown was a beauty. Corey Dailey moved us 85 yards in 10 plays late in the second quarter, hit Malik Knight for 28 deep down the left side and found Ja'Kyrian Turner for an 11-yard score to put us up 7-6 at the half. Turner finished with seven catches.

Then came the play that stung. On our second snap of the third quarter, a throw was intercepted at our 39, and five plays later Florida State was in the end zone. Antonio Chadha's 34-yard field goal pulled us to 13-10, but their kicker answered from 47 with 6:27 left.

We had our chances. Three times we went for it on fourth down and came up short, including a sack near midfield with 8:44 left. After a 64-yard punt pinned us at our own 2 with 1:49 to go, Dailey took off for 24 yards on the first snap and got us to their 48, but the last fourth-down throw fell incomplete with 43 seconds left. Dailey ran for 58 yards on nine carries and battled every snap.

Pittsburgh doesn't do quit. We're still 6-4, still 5-2 at home, and cold November football is our kind of weather. Three rivers, one city, and a whole lot of fight left in this bunch.

Next: at Louisville, Saturday, Nov. 21, kickoff time to be announced. Wear the blue and gold, make some noise on the road, and let's bring one home. Hail to Pitt.

articles.title: Florida State vs Pittsburgh: Panikowski and a Stingy Defense Win 16-10
articles.byline: Gianna Ravello, The Florida State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Florida State Seminoles (5-5) 16, Pittsburgh Panthers (6-4) 10, Fri., Nov. 13, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh. Next: vs NC State, Sat., Nov. 21, 3:30 PM ET, Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee
articles.text:
Garnet and gold just froze out Pittsburgh. Florida State 16, Pittsburgh 10 on Friday night at Acrisure Stadium, and the Seminoles are 5-5. I packed my one Tallahassee sweater for a November night on the North Shore, and I would wear it every week for wins like this.

Gabe Panikowski was the coolest man in western Pennsylvania. He hit from 37 and 27 yards in the first half, then drilled a 47-yarder with 6:27 left to make it 16-10. Three tries, three makes. Somebody put that young man's right leg in a museum.

The turning point came on Pittsburgh's second snap of the third quarter. We trailed 7-6 at the half, and Rylan Kennedy jumped a throw at the Pitt 39 and brought it back to the 32. Amari Thomas ripped off 16 yards on the very next play, and five snaps after the takeaway, Thomas punched it in from a yard out. 13-7, Noles, and I was hollering in a sea of Pitt gold.

Ashton Daniels kept the offense steady, going 16 of 24 for 163 yards with no interceptions. Jasen Lopez caught five balls for 72 yards, including a 46-yard grab down the left side that set up our second field goal.

But this one belongs to the defense. Pittsburgh converted 5 of 15 third downs and came up empty on three different fourth downs. Caleb LaVallee sacked Corey Dailey on fourth down near midfield with 8:44 left. Then Daniel Hughes boomed a 64-yard punt that pinned Pitt at its own 2 with 1:49 to go, and Charles Lester III broke up a deep ball on that last drive before the final fourth-down throw fell incomplete with 43 seconds left. Chris Jones led us with seven tackles, and CJ Richard Jr. and Ashlynd Barker had six apiece.

It wasn't pretty everywhere. We ran for 97 yards on 33 carries and lost a fumble at their 12 early in the fourth. A road win in Pittsburgh in November is a road win, though, and I will take gritty and happy every single time.

Next: NC State comes to Doak Campbell Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 3:30 PM ET. Sweater off, sunscreen on. Tallahassee, get loud.

articles.title: Colorado vs Houston: 28 Straight Points and a Stampede Onto Folsom Field
articles.matchup: Final: Colorado Buffaloes (4-6) 42, Houston Cougars (7-3) 32, Fri., Nov. 13, Folsom Field, Boulder. Next: at Cincinnati, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati
articles.text:
The kids rushed the field at Folsom, and I was right behind them with my knees creaking. Colorado 42, Houston 32 on Friday night in Boulder. The Buffaloes are 4-6, and we just beat a top-15 team for the first time since 2007. The Flatirons were dark, the air was cold, and I have never felt warmer in my life.

It did not start pretty. Houston kicked a field goal, scored again seconds into the second quarter, and was up 20-7 after a 52-yard kick with 2:36 left in the half. I was muttering at the scoreboard. Then the Go-Go offense finally went, went.

DeKalon Taylor took one carry and turned it into a 67-yard touchdown with 1:49 left. JaQuail Smith ripped off a 32-yarder with 15 seconds on the clock, and suddenly we led 21-20 at halftime. Richard Young had already gone 38 yards for our first score, and he finished with 99 yards on 21 carries and two touchdowns. Colorado ran for 249 yards, the most of the Sanders era. Boulder, we can run the ball!

The third quarter was the knockout. Right after Randon Fontenette forced a fumble on Houston's first snap of the half, Isaac Wilson hit Joseph Williams for a 53-yard touchdown, and after Wilson limped off, Kaneal Sweetwyne scored on his very first snap, a 14-yard keeper that made it 35-20. Twenty-eight straight points. Wilson finished 17 of 25 for 217 yards, and he came back on that ankle, which tells you everything about the kid.

Randon Fontenette was the best player on the field on defense. Thirteen tackles, 12 of them solo, plus that sack that knocked the ball loose from Conner Weigman. Boo Carter picked off a throw late in the third. We converted 10 of 14 third downs, and that is how you keep a good offense on the sideline.

Houston kept coming. Weigman threw for 272 yards and three scores, and when they made it 35-26, my heart did a little dance I didn't enjoy. Young's 2-yard run with 3:59 left settled it.

Two more to go, Buffs. Ralphie's ready. So am I. The Colorado Buffaloes travel to face Cincinnati in Cincinnati, Nov. 21, noon ET.

articles.title: Houston vs Colorado: Weigman Battles, Cougars Fall 42-32 in Boulder
articles.matchup: Final: Colorado Buffaloes (4-6) 42, Houston Cougars (7-3) 32, Fri., Nov. 13, Folsom Field, Boulder. Next: at West Virginia, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Milan Puskar Stadium, Morgantown
articles.text:
Coogs, I need a minute. Colorado 42, Houston 32 on Friday night at Folsom Field, and we're 7-3. I wore my red in the Boulder cold, I watched the Buffaloes fans pour onto the field, and I drove the long way back to the hotel so I could think about what happened between the last two minutes of the first half and the end of the third quarter.

Because for a while, this was our night. Jonathan Dimas opened with a 27-yard field goal. Makhi Hughes punched in an 8-yarder seconds into the second quarter. Conner Weigman hit Amare Thomas for a 4-yard score, and then Dimas drilled a 52-yarder with 2:36 left in the half. 20-7, Houston. The mountains looked friendlier at that moment.

Then it all slipped away. Colorado broke a 67-yard run, then a 32-yarder with 15 seconds left, and we went to the locker room down 21-20. On our first snap of the third quarter, Weigman got sacked and fumbled, and they cashed it in with a 53-yard throw. We came up empty on fourth down at their 25, then they added a 14-yard keeper, and that was 28 straight points against a defense I'd put up with anybody's.

I'm proud of how the offense answered. Weigman threw for 272 yards and three touchdowns. Patrick Overmyer was terrific with nine catches for 116 yards and a 22-yard score. Hughes ran for 106 yards on 15 carries, and Re'Shaun Sanford II added 70. Trent Walker caught a 4-yard touchdown with 1:51 left. We put up 477 yards in their building.

On defense, Kentrell Webb made nine tackles and Javion White picked off a throw to open the second half. But Colorado ran for 249 yards and converted 10 of 14 third downs, and nobody wins in the mountains giving up that.

This one stings because it was there for the taking. But this team is 7-3, Willie Fritz has built something real, and a single bad stretch in Boulder doesn't change that.

Bring a coat, Coogs. Then bring the fight. Go Coogs. The Houston Cougars travel to face West Virginia in Morgantown, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: UCLA vs Illinois: Scooter Jackson, Aidan Mizell and a Rain-Soaked 10-0
articles.matchup: Final: UCLA Bruins (10-0) 22, Illinois Fighting Illini (6-4) 14, Fri., Nov. 13, Rose Bowl, Pasadena. Next: at Michigan, Sat., Nov. 21, time TBA, Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor
articles.text:
Ten and oh. Say it slowly, Westwood. UCLA 22, Illinois 14 on Friday night at the Rose Bowl, and the Bruins are 10-0 for the third time in program history. It rained in Pasadena, which basically never happens, and I stood in the Arroyo with a soggy blue poncho and the biggest grin in Southern California.

Let's start with Aidan Mizell, because the man refuses to be slowed by anything, rain included. Six catches, 176 yards. On our opening drive he hauled in a 54-yard touchdown from Ty Dieffenbach, and the whole stadium knew right away this was going to be his night.

Then came the scare. Dieffenbach went down on that elbow late in the second quarter and headed to the locker room, and I swear you could hear 45,800 people hold their breath at once. Madden Iamaleava kept the ship upright for three series. When Ty jogged back onto the field with 55 seconds left in the third, the noise was something I will tell my grandkids about. His first drive back went 75 yards in eight plays and ended with Semaj Morgan catching a 26-yarder in the end zone. 19-7, Bruins. Dieffenbach finished 13 of 20 for 232 yards and two scores. Warrior stuff.

But the best part of this whole wet night was the defense. Scooter Jackson picked off two throws, including the one with 2:50 left that he took back 41 yards to the Illinois 19. Derrick Barksdale grabbed another. Aiden Gobaira sacked Katin Houser in the end zone for a safety in the third quarter, and Sammy Omosigho led us with seven tackles. Illinois managed 240 yards and 64 on the ground. Seven straight opponents held to 20 points or fewer. Pasadena, that's a wall.

Mateen Bhaghani was perfect, too: a 20-yarder before halftime and a 37-yarder with 1:56 left that made it a two-score game. Curtis Gerrand dropped three punts inside the 20. Special teams win wet games.

Illinois never quit, I'll give the Illini that. They cut it to 19-14 with 7:14 to go, and I was not breathing again for a while. But this group just keeps finding a way.

Big House, big stage, 10-0 Bruins. Pack a sweater, Westwood. We're going to need it. The UCLA Bruins travel to face Michigan in Ann Arbor, Nov. 21, time TBA.

articles.title: Illinois vs UCLA: Illini Fight Back in the Rain, Fall 22-14 in Pasadena
articles.matchup: Final: UCLA Bruins (10-0) 22, Illinois Fighting Illini (6-4) 14, Fri., Nov. 13, Rose Bowl, Pasadena. Next: vs Iowa, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET, Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign
articles.text:
Well, Illini Nation, we came to the Rose Bowl and it rained on us. Of course it did. UCLA 22, Illinois 14 on Friday night in Pasadena, and we're 6-4. I flew out of Champaign hoping for sunshine and palm trees and got a wet seat and a long walk back to the car.

The first half was rough, and there's no use pretending otherwise. UCLA hit a 54-yard touchdown on its first drive, kicked a field goal before halftime, and we went into the locker room down 10-0 without a point to show for our trouble. Then in the third quarter Katin Houser got sacked in the end zone for a safety, and it was 12-0. That's when you find out what a team is made of.

Ours is made of fight. Late in the third, Houser found Kaden Feagin for an 18-yard touchdown, and the orange in our corner of the stadium came alive. After UCLA answered, Houser marched us right back and hit Collin Dixon from 7 yards out with 7:14 left. 19-14. We were one stop and one drive from stealing one at the Rose Bowl.

James Kreutz played like a man possessed. Eleven tackles, three for loss, and he seemed to be in on every big stop. Matthew Bailey added nine tackles, Ismael Kante got a sack, and Clarke picked off a throw in our end zone in the second quarter to keep it close. That defense deserved better than this result.

The turnovers are what got us. Houser threw three interceptions, two to Scooter Jackson, and the last one came with 2:50 left and the game still in reach. UCLA kicked a 37-yarder at 1:56, and our last try ended on a fourth-down throw that fell incomplete. Hudson Clement had three catches for 62 yards and Aidan Laughery ran hard for 49, but against an unbeaten team, three giveaways are too many.

Here's what I know about this program. We went into the Rose Bowl against an unbeaten team and made them sweat into the final two minutes. We converted 8 of 16 on third down. Nobody packed it in.

Dry socks, loud voices. Oskee-wow-wow, Champaign. The Illinois Fighting Illini host Iowa at Gies Memorial Stadium, Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET.

articles.title: New York Giants vs Washington Commanders Week 10: 57 Seconds From a Win, 21-24
articles.matchup: Final: Washington Commanders (3-5-1) 24, New York Giants (5-3-1) 21, Thu., Nov. 12, MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford. Next: vs Jacksonville Jaguars, Sun., Nov. 22, 4:25 PM ET, MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford
articles.text:
Fifty-seven seconds. That's how close we were. Washington 24, New York 21 on Thursday night at MetLife Stadium, and 80,450 of us walked out to the parking lots stunned. We're 5-3-1 and still sitting first in the NFC East, but this one is going to sting all weekend.

Cam Skattebo ran like a man who'd been insulted. He capped a 16-play, 72-yard drive with a 1-yard plunge in the second quarter and bounced in from 13 in the third for a 14-10 lead. Two touchdowns and 78 yards on 18 carries, and every one of them hurt somebody.

Isaiah Likely was the best player on the field. Nine catches, 127 yards, and on third-and-7 from our 34 he ran right through the middle of their defense for a 66-yard touchdown. 21-17 Giants with 8:13 left. J.J. McCarthy finished 23 of 36 for 293 yards.

And the secondary went to work. Jevon Holland intercepted Jayden Daniels at our 2, and Ar'Darius Washington took another one away on fourth down at their 46 with 2:19 to go. Arvell Reese made 13 tackles, Micah McFadden had 10, and Shelby Harris sacked Daniels for a 14-yard loss in the third quarter.

Then the last two minutes. Our punt from their 41 went just 12 yards. A 33-yard interference flag put Washington in business, and Stefon Diggs caught a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. We still had a chance, but McCarthy's deep throw for Malik Nabers was intercepted at their 11.

A few leftovers will keep me up tonight. Dominic Zvada missed a 33-yarder wide left in the first quarter, and Nabers lost a fumble inside their 20 in the third. Those are points left on the field in a three-point game.

Next: the Jacksonville Jaguars at MetLife on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:25 PM ET. First place is still ours. Let's go keep it. Go Big Blue.

articles.title: Washington Commanders vs New York Giants Week 10: Diggs With 57 Seconds Left, 24-21
articles.matchup: Final: Washington Commanders (3-5-1) 24, New York Giants (5-3-1) 21, Thu., Nov. 12, MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford. Next: vs Cincinnati Bengals, Mon., Nov. 23, 8:15 PM ET, Northwest Stadium, Landover
articles.text:
Hail to the Commanders, and somebody please check on my voice. Washington 24, New York 21 on Thursday night at MetLife Stadium, and we took this one in front of 80,450 people who wanted any other ending. We're 3-5-1, and that last minute felt like a whole season.

It was a slugfest for a half. Drew Stevens opened the scoring from 46 yards. The Giants answered with a 16-play march that ate 7:48 and ended with a Cam Skattebo plunge, but Jayden Daniels took us 67 yards in nine plays and flipped it to Ben Sinnott from a yard out with five seconds left in the half. 10-7, us.

Skattebo scored again from 13 early in the third to put them ahead 14-10. Daniels answered on third-and-1, hitting Antonio Williams for a 31-yard touchdown. 17-14. Then Frankie Luvu punched the ball loose from Malik Nabers inside our 20, and Jeremy Reaves fell on it. Reaves had nine tackles and was everywhere all night.

The fourth quarter tried to break my heart. We came up empty on fourth-and-1 at their 30. Isaiah Likely took a catch 66 yards to give New York a 21-17 lead with 8:13 left. Daniels got intercepted twice, once at their 2 by Jevon Holland and once on fourth down by Ar'Darius Washington. I sat down. I stood up. I sat down again.

Then their punt from our 41 went 12 yards and out of bounds, and we had it at our 29 with 1:46 to go. A 33-yard interference flag got us moving, and on third-and-4 Daniels found Stefon Diggs down the middle for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. Three plays, 71 yards, 49 seconds. Rasul Douglas sealed it by intercepting J.J. McCarthy at our 11 with 34 seconds left.

Daniels finished 23 of 33 for 249 yards and three touchdowns. Diggs caught six for 83. Sonny Styles made 13 tackles, Odafe Oweh had a sack, and Tress Way averaged 49.5 yards on four punts. That tie with these same Giants back in October at Northwest Stadium? Consider it settled.

Next up: the Cincinnati Bengals at Northwest Stadium on Monday, Nov. 23, 8:15 PM ET. Rest up, fellas. HTTR.

articles.title: South Florida vs Memphis: The Bulls Climb Out of a 21-0 Hole and Fall Short 52-41
articles.byline: Reina Valdés-Kowalski, The South Florida Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Memphis Tigers (8-2) 52, South Florida Bulls (6-4) 41, Thu., Nov. 12, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa. Next: at Florida Atlantic, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET, Flagler Credit Union Stadium, Boca Raton
articles.text:
I'm hoarse, I'm heartbroken, and I'm proud of this team. Memphis 52, South Florida 41 at Raymond James Stadium on Thursday night, and the Bulls are 6-4. That one hurts, but nobody in green and gold quit.

The first quarter was a nightmare. Memphis scored three times, a fumble at our 21 handed them the third one, and we trailed 21-0 before the first quarter ended. Lots of teams fold right there. Not ours.

Luke Kromenhoek put this whole team on his back. He ran 30 times for 146 yards, threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns, and never threw an interception. Mudia Reuben caught two of those scores, a 3-yarder on fourth down and a 19-yarder with 49 seconds left in the half, and finished with six catches for 98 yards. We went into the locker room down 28-17 and alive again.

The third quarter was pure Tampa thunder. Jason Collins Jr. caught a 13-yard touchdown, then answered a Memphis score on the very next snap with a 75-yard run up the middle. Kromenhoek ran in from 23 to tie it 38-38. Nico Gramatica, perfect on two field goals and five extra points, hit from 38 to give us a 41-38 lead with 8:04 left. Herlin Perry Jr. broke up a Stokes pass at our 8 to force a field goal.

Then it slipped away. Memphis hit a 76-yarder two plays later, and our drive to answer reached their 4 before a fourth-down throw fell incomplete with 3:38 left. Seven sacks were the other story, and that front got to Kromenhoek again on our last real chance.

Look at what this team did, though. We gained 552 yards with 29 first downs, held the ball for 37:35 and converted five of eight fourth downs. Israel Boyce had a sack, and Joshua Porter set up a field goal with a 36-yard punt return.

Next: at Florida Atlantic, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET, in Boca Raton. Bring that same fire down to Boca, Bulls. I'll be there, loud as ever.

articles.title: Memphis vs South Florida: Marcus Stokes Has a Hand in Five Scores and the Tigers Go to 8-2
articles.matchup: Final: Memphis Tigers (8-2) 52, South Florida Bulls (6-4) 41, Thu., Nov. 12, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa. Next: at Navy, Sat., Nov. 21, 12:00 PM ET, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, Annapolis
articles.text:
Somebody bring Tampa a mop. Memphis 52, South Florida 41 on Thursday night at Raymond James Stadium, and the Tigers are 8-2. I flew down expecting a fight, and brother, we got one.

It opened like a parade. Marcus Stokes kept it up the middle on our first drive and outran the whole Bulls secondary to the end zone. Then he found Hunter Tipton from 7 yards. Then Jabari Ishmael jumped on a South Florida fumble at their 21, and four plays later Stokes ran it in from 8. Memphis 21, South Florida 0, and the first quarter hadn't even ended.

Then those Bulls got up off the mat. Luke Kromenhoek ran 30 times and threw for three scores, Jason Collins Jr. went 75 yards on one snap, and by late in the third it was 38-38. With 8:04 left, Nico Gramatica put them ahead 41-38. My heart was somewhere in Hillsborough County.

Two snaps. That's all it took. Stokes dropped back from our 24 and launched one deep right to Jemyri Davis, who caught it in stride and was gone. 76 yards. 45-41. Davis finished with five catches for 161 yards, and I may name my next dog after him.

And then the defense won it. South Florida drove to our 4 and went for it on fourth down, and the throw fell incomplete with 3:38 to go. They got the ball back one more time, and J'Mond Tapp and Elijah Kinsler chased Kromenhoek all around the backfield until it died on fourth-and-27. Jaylin Carter then broke a 26-yard run for the clincher with 44 seconds left. Carter finished with 109 yards and two scores on 21 carries.

Stokes went 15 of 31 for 313 yards and three touchdowns with zero interceptions, and he added 73 yards and two more scores on the ground. That's a hand in five touchdowns. We piled up 581 yards with zero turnovers. Our front had seven sacks, with Tapp at two and a half and Kinsler at two. Mike Montgomery made 19 tackles, which I believe is every tackle available in the state of Florida.

Next stop is Navy, Saturday, Nov. 21, at noon ET in Annapolis. Pack the parkas. Eight wins and counting, and I'm not done hollering.

articles.title: UL Monroe vs Louisiana: Warhawks Strike First, Fall 42-21 at Malone
articles.byline: Darnell Vidrine, The UL Monroe Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns (7-3) 42, UL Monroe Warhawks (2-8) 21, Thu., Nov. 12, Malone Stadium, Monroe. Next: at App State, Sat., Nov. 21, 2:30 PM ET, Boone, N.C.
articles.text:
Malone Stadium was rocking early, and for one half the Warhawks had the Cajuns in a real fight. Louisiana 42, UL Monroe 21 on Thursday night in Monroe, and we're 2-8, but don't let that final fool you about how hard these guys played.

Our opening drive was a work of art: 15 plays, 73 yards, 8:18 off the clock, and Austin Carlisle pushing in from a yard out. After Louisiana tied it, 24-yard runs from Carlisle and Bryson Roland set up a 5-yard scoring throw from Carlisle to Jaiden Tucker, and we led 14-7 early in the second quarter.

That was Warhawks football the way folks along the Ouachita River like it. Carlisle carried 21 times for 102 yards, Roland went for 111 on 17 carries, and we held the ball for 35:27. We moved the chains on 9 of 17 third downs and outgained Louisiana 372 yards to 339.

The trouble was the football itself. Our late first-half drive ended with an interception at their 13 with five seconds left. Then a fumble early in the third went back 18 yards for a Louisiana score, and another fumble at our own 19 turned into a touchdown on the very next snap. Three turnovers, 14 points off them, and a 14-14 game became 28-14.

From there JJ Garner and Steven Blanco did what fast backs do, and Louisiana ran for 274 yards. I won't pretend that part was fun to watch from my seat.

But these Warhawks never quit. Down 35-14, with Aidan Armenta at quarterback, we marched 75 yards in 15 plays. Facing fourth-and-10 near midfield, Armenta found Bryce Anderson for 27 yards, and Don Chaney finished it from 6 yards out to make it 35-21. Jabari Tiller made nine tackles and Chris Payne made seven, and nobody in maroon and gold stopped hitting.

Next: at App State, Saturday, Nov. 21, at 2:30 PM ET in Boone. It's a long trip to the mountains, so pack a coat and bring that opening-drive energy for all four quarters. Warhawk fans, I'll see you there, loud as ever.

Lunch Winfield answered with a 13-yard strike to Shelton Sampson Jr., ULM went back ahead 14-7, and then KeDarius Wade slipped in from 8 yards with 40 seconds left in the half to tie it. Kody Jackson intercepted a throw at our 13 five seconds before the break, and I hugged a complete stranger.

Then our defense took charge of the whole parish. Early in the third, Micah Johnson scooped up a Warhawks fumble and rumbled 18 yards to the end zone for a 21-14 lead. A few series later, Maurion Eleam punched the ball loose, Johnson fell on it at the ULM 19, and JJ Garner went 19 yards on the very next snap. 28-14, and the Cajun side of the stadium was dancing.

Garner was the lightning all night. Nine carries, 104 yards, two scores, including an 18-yarder early in the fourth that made it 35-14. Steven Blanco was the thunder, with 113 yards on 15 carries. After ULM answered to make it 35-21, Blanco carried on all six snaps of a 50-yard drive, had a score wiped out by a flag, shrugged, and walked in from 2 yards anyway with 1:57 left.

We ran for 274 yards on 33 carries and gave the ball away zero times. One Warhawks fumble went the other way for six, and another turned into six more on the next snap. Jake St. Andre made 14 tackles, Collin Jacob made nine, and Johnson had nine to go with that touchdown.

Credit to Monroe, though. Those Warhawks ran it right at us, held the ball for 35:27 and kept swinging into the fourth quarter. Bryson Roland and Carlisle both cleared 100 yards on the ground. But the bragging rights ride back down to Acadiana with us tonight.

Next up, Coastal Carolina visits Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium in Lafayette on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 3:00 PM ET. Come hungry, come loud, and wear that vermilion. Seven wins, and the gumbo is still simmering.

articles.title: UMass vs Toledo: Shut Out at the Glass Bowl, but Timmy Hinspeter Never Stopped Hitting
articles.matchup: Final: Massachusetts Minutemen (5-5) 0, Toledo Rockets (8-2) 24, Wed., Nov. 11, Glass Bowl, Toledo. Next: vs Akron, Wed., Nov. 18, 7:00 PM ET, Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium, Amherst
articles.text:
Some nights you write in the diary, and some nights you tear the page out. Toledo 24, UMass 0 at the Glass Bowl on Wednesday night, and the Minutemen are 5-5. I watched every snap, and I'm going to tell you about the good parts, because there were some.

The second half was ours. Toledo scored zero points after halftime. The Rockets had six possessions in the second half, and our defense answered with four punts, a stop on fourth down and a clock that ran out. That's how you play in November.

Timmy Hinspeter was everywhere: 12 tackles, one of them for a loss. Kendall Bournes added eight, Tyler Martin had five, and Joshua Nobles made a tackle for loss of his own. That group didn't hang its head once.

The first half was the problem. Connor Walendzak broke a 69-yard run, Reice Griffith kicked a 27-yarder, and then Nicholas Thompson intercepted Logan Inagawa and returned it 62 yards. Walendzak caught a 17-yard score before the break, and it was 24-0 at halftime.

Inagawa kept swinging. He ran for 40 yards, including an 18-yarder, and Reece Adkins caught five balls for 33 yards. Drew Alsup had a 19-yard grab. Our best march went 11 plays and 53 yards late in the third quarter, and it ended on fourth down. So close to the board I could taste it.

Toledo held us to 188 yards, we converted 3 of 15 third downs, and we drew five flags for 50 yards. Not good enough, and everybody in maroon knows it. The good news is the defense gave us a blueprint for the second half of every game left.

We're 5-5 with Akron coming to Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at 7:00 PM ET. Home cooking in Amherst. Let's go get one, Minutemen.

articles.title: Toledo vs UMass: A Glass Bowl Shutout and the Rockets Go to 8-2
articles.matchup: Final: Massachusetts Minutemen (5-5) 0, Toledo Rockets (8-2) 24, Wed., Nov. 11, Glass Bowl, Toledo. Next: vs Bowling Green, Fri., Nov. 20, 7:30 PM ET, Glass Bowl, Toledo
articles.text:
Zero. Paint it on a sign and hang it off the Anthony Wayne Bridge. Toledo 24, UMass 0 at the Glass Bowl on Wednesday night in front of 19,137, and the Rockets are 8-2 and 5-1 in the MAC.

Connor Walendzak lit the fuse. First quarter, he took a handoff 69 yards to the house to finish a five-play, 90-yard drive. Second quarter, he caught a 17-yard throw from John Alan Richter for another. He piled up 117 rushing yards on 14 carries and 41 more receiving. That kid is a problem for the whole conference.

Reice Griffith hit a 27-yard field goal early in the second quarter, and then came the play I'll be telling my grandkids about. Nicholas Thompson jumped a throw and went 62 yards the other way for a touchdown. 17-0 with 10:32 left in the half, and the Glass Bowl shook.

Adjatay Dabbs caught seven balls for 144 yards with a long of 40. Richter went 13 of 22 for 197 yards and didn't throw an interception. CJ Miller ground out 83 yards on 15 carries. Our offense put up 436 yards, averaged 9.0 yards per throw, and held the ball for 34:33. That is Rocket football the way it was drawn up.

But this is a defense story. UMass managed 188 yards and 10 first downs, converted 3 of 15 third downs, and came up empty on fourth down three times. Julian Fox had eight tackles, three of them for a loss. Andrew Zock had two sacks and three tackles for loss. Donovan Watkins broke up two throws. That's a shutout earned snap by snap.

Gripe time: 10 penalties for 90 yards, and no points after halftime. That second half needs work before the next one, because the next one matters.

Next: Bowling Green at the Glass Bowl, Friday, Nov. 20, 7:30 PM ET. The Battle of I-75. Fill every seat, Toledo.

articles.title: Ball State vs Buffalo: A Blocked Punt, Three Missed Kicks and a Long Night in Muncie
articles.byline: Gus Ponder, The Ball State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Buffalo Bulls (7-3) 28, Ball State Cardinals (3-7) 7, Wed., Nov. 11, Scheumann Stadium, Muncie. Next: at Ohio, Tue., Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, Peden Stadium, Athens
articles.text:
I'll say it first so nobody else has to. Buffalo 28, Ball State 7 at Scheumann Stadium on Wednesday night, and the Cardinals are 3-7. I've sat in these seats through rough ones, but this one stings, because we had our chances.

And it opened like a dream. Late in the first quarter our special teams got a hand on a Buffalo punt, and Gabe Aramboles recovered it in the end zone. 7-0, and the home crowd of 6,745 was loud.

Then came the kicks. Brody Boehm tried from 47, 44 and 39 yards, and none of them went through. That's nine points we left on the field in a game that was tied 7-7 at the half.

The effort was there. Donovan Hamilton was a workhorse with 11 catches for 104 yards. Keldric Luster threw it 39 times and kept firing. TJ Horton ran 11 times for 92 yards. We gained 325 yards, Buffalo gained 350, and the scoreboard still said what it said.

The fourth quarter opened with our best drive of the night, nine plays and 75 yards, and it died on fourth down at the Buffalo 22. Then Messiah Burch went 67 yards, Buffalo recovered an onside kick, and Terrance Shelton Jr. went 29 more. Burch finished with 209 yards on 31 carries. Tip of the cap. Reluctantly.

Our defense hung in for three quarters. Sterling Smith had 10 tackles, Jared Badie had two sacks, and Mikeah Webster added another. Buffalo completed five throws all night for 48 yards. Keep that Bulls quarterback in the pocket and we can play with anybody in this league.

Next: at Ohio, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, at Peden Stadium in Athens. Practice those kicks, Cardinals. Put three of them through and this one looks a whole lot different. I'll be in Athens either way, loud as ever.

articles.title: Buffalo vs Ball State: Messiah Burch Runs for 209 and the Bulls Go to 7-3
articles.matchup: Final: Buffalo Bulls (7-3) 28, Ball State Cardinals (3-7) 7, Wed., Nov. 11, Scheumann Stadium, Muncie. Next: vs Central Michigan, Wed., Nov. 18, 7:30 PM ET, Broadview Stadium, Buffalo
articles.text:
Pack a lunch, Muncie. Buffalo 28, Ball State 7 on Wednesday night at Scheumann Stadium, and the Bulls are 7-3 and 5-1 in the MAC. We ran the ball 52 times for 302 yards. I counted every carry from the visitors' side, and my mittens are done for the season.

The night opened crooked. Ball State blocked one of our punts late in the first quarter, and Gabe Aramboles fell on it in the end zone. 7-0 Cardinals. Fine. We do our best work from behind.

Jason Wright answered with an 11-play, 80-yard drive in the second quarter and finished it with a 14-yard throw to Chance Morrow. 7-7. Wright completed five throws all night, and he didn't need more. This team knows exactly who it is.

Who it is, mostly, is Messiah Burch. He carried 31 times for 209 yards and two scores. His 2-yard run capped a 12-play, 79-yard drive in the third for a 14-7 lead. Then, with 4:04 left, he found a crease up the middle and went 67 yards. 21-7.

And then the coaches got bold. Oliver Hautanen popped an onside kick, we came up with it at the Ball State 29, and Terrance Shelton Jr. went 29 yards on the very next snap. Two touchdowns in six seconds of game clock. 28-7. Shelton finished with 92 yards on 10 carries.

The defense deserves its own parade down Main Street. Ball State came away empty on fourth down three times, twice inside our 25 in the fourth quarter, and three Cardinals field goal tries, from 47, 44 and 39 yards, did not go through. SaVeon Brown and Zach Bergmann had nine tackles each, Mikey Crawford had eight, and Miles Greer chipped in a tackle for loss. Zero turnovers for us, too.

Next up is Central Michigan at Broadview Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at 7:30 PM ET. Bring the hand warmers. We're bringing the run game.

articles.title: Sacramento State vs Central Michigan: Isaiah Ene's 37-Yard Dash and a Long Night in Mount Pleasant
articles.byline: Mateo Villaseñor, The Sacramento State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Sacramento State Hornets (2-9) 7, Central Michigan Chippewas (5-5) 28, Wed., Nov. 11, Mount Pleasant. Next: at Hawai'i, Sat., Nov. 28, 11:00 PM ET, Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex, Honolulu
articles.text:
A long way from home, on a Wednesday night in Michigan, the Hornets took the field and swung. Central Michigan 28, Sacramento State 7. We're 2-9. I'm still wearing the green and gold, and I'm not taking it off.

The first drive looked like us. Brian Salazar Jr. moved the ball 66 yards in 10 plays, all the way to the Central Michigan 16, and then Justin Taylor intercepted a throw at the 7. Heartbreaker. Points there and this is a different night.

Isaiah Ene was the bright spot. Second quarter, four plays and 68 yards, and Ene went the last 37 himself to tie it 7-7. He finished with 67 yards on eight carries and caught two balls. Give that man the ball more. I'm begging.

The defense worked all night long. Leki Holani made 14 tackles. Boogsie Silvera had 11 and forced a fumble that Miles Tucker recovered at our 38. Tim Thomas added nine tackles, a tackle for loss and two hurries. Those guys never quit.

But Central Michigan had the ball for 39:48 and ran it 56 times. Vaughn Blue scored with 19 seconds left in the half, Brock Townsend broke a 40-yarder in the third, and Townsend added a late one. We finished with 211 yards and 10 first downs, and that's the whole story.

Onterrio Smith Jr. led us with four catches for 47 yards, including a 25-yarder, and Davion Godley ripped off a 23-yard run. There's talent on this roster. Ask anybody who stuck around to the end. Salazar took his hits and kept getting up, and that matters to me more than any stat sheet.

Now we get a breather, then one more trip west: at Hawai'i, Saturday, Nov. 28, 11:00 PM ET, at the Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex in Honolulu. Long flight. Let's finish strong, Hornets.

articles.title: Central Michigan vs Sacramento State: 319 Rushing Yards and the Chippewas Climb to 5-5
articles.byline: Brynn Haverkamp, The Central Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Sacramento State Hornets (2-9) 7, Central Michigan Chippewas (5-5) 28, Wed., Nov. 11, Mount Pleasant. Next: at Buffalo, Wed., Nov. 18, 7:30 PM ET, Broadview Stadium, Buffalo
articles.text:
Fifty-six carries. 319 yards. 39:48 of possession. Central Michigan 28, Sacramento State 7 on Wednesday night in Mount Pleasant, and the Chippewas are back to 5-5 and 3-3 in the MAC. Maroon and gold, ground and pound, exactly how I drew it up on my napkin at dinner.

Jayden Clerveaux set the tone on the very first drive, seven plays and 68 yards, and he finished it himself with a 27-yard run. He ended with 100 yards on 19 carries. Nick Woodford led everybody with 119 yards on 23 carries. Two backs, two hundreds. Somebody frame that box score.

Sacramento State answered with a long march down to our 16, and then Justin Taylor stepped in front of a Brian Salazar Jr. throw at our 7. Drive done. That's a game-changing play nobody will remember but me.

The Hornets did get one. Isaiah Ene went 37 yards in the second quarter to tie it 7-7. Our answer was an 11-play, 71-yard drive, and Vaughn Blue ran it in from 8 yards out with 19 seconds left in the half.

Then came the drive of the year. Twelve plays, 97 yards, and Brock Townsend finished it with a 40-yard run in the third quarter. He added a 6-yard score late and had 58 yards on five carries. Every time that kid touches it, Mount Pleasant gets louder.

Jadyn Glasser ran the show: 11 of 19 for 105 yards, no interceptions, plus 33 yards on the ground. Nasir Williams hauled in a 52-yarder. We converted 11 of 18 third downs and 3 of 4 fourth downs, and Jaion Jackson added a sack. The defense held Sac State to 211 yards and 10 first downs.

One gripe: Caden VanHuis missed from 50 and Clerveaux lost a fumble. Tidy that up, fellas, because next week is a big one.

Next: at Buffalo, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 7:30 PM ET, at Broadview Stadium. Two run-first teams in November. I'm bringing extra layers and a louder voice.

articles.title: Ohio vs Miami (OH): A 17-0 Lead Gets Away in Oxford
articles.matchup: Final: Ohio Bobcats (7-3) 17, Miami (OH) RedHawks (6-4) 34, Tue., Nov. 10, Yager Stadium, Oxford. Next: vs Ball State, Tue., Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, Peden Stadium, Athens
articles.text:
I'm going to say it once and then talk football. Ohio led Miami 17-0 in the second quarter on Tuesday night at Yager Stadium and lost the Battle of the Bricks 34-17. The six-game winning streak is done. The perfect MAC record is done. We're 7-3 and 5-1, and it's a quiet ride back to Athens.

The first quarter and a half looked like the team I love. Nick Poulos took us 75 yards in eight plays on the opening drive and hit Riley Neer for an 8-yard touchdown. Duncan Brune punched one in from the 1 early in the second quarter. Brack Peacock added a 22-yarder. Michael Molnar was living in their backfield, with a sack and 8 tackles on the night.

Then it slipped. Miami's freshman receiver Scoop Smith threw a 15-yard touchdown with 1:02 left in the half. We still drove to the Miami 18 in the final minute. Peacock's 34-yarder at the gun missed, a Miami flag gave us one more snap from the 8, and the throw from our holder was knocked down. Zero points from the 8. I would have kicked it again.

Second half: zero points. We converted 3 of 17 third downs for the game, and we had seven penalties for 44 yards, several of them flags before the snap. You can't move the chains walking backward.

And the ending. Down 20-17 with 3:55 left, we were moving, and Poulos fumbled at our own 48. Malcolm McCain took it away. D'Shawntae Jones went 48 yards on the next play. Then Amariyun Knighten intercepted Poulos and took it back 58 yards. Miami scored 20 points in the fourth quarter.

Credit where it's due. Poulos ran 17 times for 68 yards and threw for 193, Neer caught 6 balls for 74 and the touchdown, and Darren James-Hamilton and Molnar each had 8 tackles. Our defense held Miami to 10 completions in 25 tries. The giveaways beat us, not the effort.

Ohio Athletics said we came to Oxford looking for a third straight win in this series. That'll have to wait a year. Ball State comes to Peden Stadium next Tuesday, Nov. 17, at 7:00 PM ET. Hold onto the football, and the MAC race is still right in front of us.

articles.title: Miami (OH) vs Ohio: Down 17-0 on Senior Night, Then 34 Straight in the Battle of the Bricks
articles.byline: Cordelia Van Doren, The Miami (OH) Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Ohio Bobcats (7-3) 17, Miami (OH) RedHawks (6-4) 34, Tue., Nov. 10, Yager Stadium, Oxford. Next: at Kent State, Tue., Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, Zoeller Field at Dix Stadium, Kent
articles.text:
Down 17-0. At home. On Senior Night. In the Battle of the Bricks. Then the RedHawks scored the last 34 points of the night, and Miami beat Ohio 34-17 at Yager Stadium. We're 6-4 and 4-2 in the MAC, and Miami Athletics said before the game that a win would make us bowl eligible again. Done.

The turn came with 1:02 left in the first half, and it came from a receiver. Scoop Smith, the freshman, took the ball and threw 15 yards to Maleek Huggins for a touchdown. 17-7. Drew Bellisari had come in at quarterback on that drive and hit Braylon Isom twice to get us there.

Ohio still had one more chance before the break. Brack Peacock missed from 34 at the gun, our unsportsmanlike flag gave them one more snap from the 8, and they tried a throw from the holder. Blayne Myrick knocked it down. Halftime, and you could feel it turning.

Our defense pitched a shutout in the second half. Ohio converted 3 of 17 third downs all night. Bellisari ran 31 yards to the 1 to set up D'Shawntae Jones's touchdown, Brady Stidham tied it from 36 early in the fourth, and Bellisari broke a 26-yarder that set up Stidham's 25-yarder for a 20-17 lead with 3:55 left.

And then the last two minutes, which I would like framed. Malcolm McCain forced a Nick Poulos fumble and recovered it himself at the Ohio 48. Next snap, Jones went 48 yards for the touchdown. Twenty seconds later, Amariyun Knighten intercepted Poulos and returned it 58 yards for another. Yager came apart at the seams.

Jones finished with 115 yards and two touchdowns on 18 carries, a week after he ran for 112 against Buffalo. McCain had 12 tackles, CJ Young had 11, and Roosevelt Andrews III had a sack. Seniors, that's how you say goodbye to Yager.

Ohio came in on a six-game winning streak with a perfect MAC record, and The Miami Student reminded everyone that the Bobcats had won the last two meetings. Ask them how Oxford was.

Next Tuesday, Nov. 17, we're at Kent State, 7:00 PM ET at Dix Stadium.

articles.title: Kent State vs Bowling Green: A Fourth-Quarter Comeback That Lasted Nine Seconds
articles.byline: Ozzie Brannigan, The Kent State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Kent State Golden Flashes (3-7) 28, Bowling Green Falcons (3-7) 33, Tue., Nov. 10, Doyt L. Perry Stadium, Bowling Green. Next: vs Miami (OH), Tue., Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, Zoeller Field at Dix Stadium, Kent
articles.text:
I expected the worst. I got a more creative version. Kent State came back from 13 points down in the fourth quarter at Doyt L. Perry Stadium, took a 28-27 lead with 2:00 left, and lost 33-28 anyway. The lead lasted nine seconds. We're 3-7, 2-4 in the MAC, and the Anniversary Award rides back to Bowling Green.

Let me be fair, because Dru DeShields earned it. He threw for 332 yards and two touchdowns and ran for two more, including the 25-yard run that put us ahead. I was on my feet. I don't stand up for much.

Wayne Harris was the best player on the field. Eight catches, 143 yards, a 39-yard score in the second quarter for a 14-7 lead and a 13-yarder in the fourth to begin the comeback. Da'Realyst Clark added 107 yards on five catches. Those two can play with anybody in this conference.

Here's where my mood went. Early in the fourth we drove 67 yards, and DeShields was intercepted by Josira Andrews at the Bowling Green 2. Points, gone. Then there's Myles Bradley, who ESPN credits with five sacks against us. Five. We converted 5 of 17 third downs. You can't live like that.

After our go-ahead score, Bowling Green needed two plays: a 16-yard catch by Joseph Saffold and a 48-yard run by Nakai Amachree. We stopped the two-point try, which I mention only because I like to be accurate. Then DeShields got us to the Bowling Green 35, took a sack, and threw it into the end zone, where Nick Sawyer caught it. Touchback. That's the season in one sentence.

Some good news, since I'm required to look for it. Jaihien Roy had a sack and 6 tackles, Darian Blachewicz had a sack and a half, and Hayden Dawahare made 9 tackles. The defense held Bowling Green to 118 rushing yards and 6 of 14 on third down.

Next Tuesday, Nov. 17, Miami (OH) comes to Dix Stadium for a 7:00 PM ET kickoff. We haven't won on the road this year, so a home game is welcome news. I expect rain. I expect it every week.

articles.title: Bowling Green vs Kent State: Nine Seconds, 48 Yards, and the Anniversary Award Comes Home
articles.byline: Darcy Fenwick, The Bowling Green Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Kent State Golden Flashes (3-7) 28, Bowling Green Falcons (3-7) 33, Tue., Nov. 10, Doyt L. Perry Stadium, Bowling Green. Next: at Toledo, Fri., Nov. 20, 7:30 PM ET, Glass Bowl, Toledo
articles.text:
It's back. On a 51-degree Tuesday night in front of 10,254 at Doyt L. Perry Stadium, Bowling Green beat Kent State 33-28, and the Anniversary Award comes home after a year in Kent. That trophy was made in 1985 to honor two schools born the same year, 1910. It belongs on our side of the state. The Falcons are 3-7, 3-3 in the MAC, and I have no voice left.

Austin Novosad ran our offense from the first snap for the first time in his career, per the AP, and needed three plays to find Nakai Amachree for 70 yards and a touchdown. Novosad finished 15 of 25 for 229 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. Eli Jacon-Duffy caught a 23-yarder, Blane Cleaver caught a 1-yarder, and Travis Kenner hit from 46 with two seconds left in the half and from 38 in the third.

Myles Bradley. ESPN credits him with five sacks. Five! Kent State's quarterback is going to see number 23 when he closes his eyes tonight. Eriq George added a sack and a half, and Dorian Pringle made 10 tackles.

Now the part that took a year off my life. We led 27-14 going into the fourth quarter, and Kent State came all the way back. Wayne Harris caught a 13-yard score, then Dru DeShields ran 25 yards to put them up 28-27 with 2:00 left. My heart stopped.

Nine seconds. That's how long it lasted. Novosad hit Joseph Saffold for 16, and Amachree took the handoff left and went 48 yards to the end zone with 1:51 to go. The two-point try failed, so it was 33-28 and the defense had to finish it.

And it did. Josira Andrews had already intercepted DeShields at our 2 early in the fourth. On Kent State's last drive, with 54 seconds left and George in DeShields's face, Nick Sawyer intercepted him in the end zone. Ballgame. Trophy.

Amachree, by the way: 110 rushing yards, 87 receiving yards, two touchdowns. Somebody bake that man a cake.

Next is Friday, Nov. 20, at Toledo, 7:30 PM ET in the Glass Bowl. The Anniversary Award stays in Wood County. Let's go get some more hardware.

articles.title: Akron vs Western Michigan: Marcel Williams Bounces Back Twice in a 42-14 Loss
articles.matchup: Final: Western Michigan Broncos (7-3) 42, Akron Zips (1-9) 14, Tue., Nov. 10, InfoCision Stadium, Akron. Next: at Massachusetts, Wed., Nov. 18, 7:00 PM ET, Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium, Amherst
articles.text:
I'm not going to dress this one up. Western Michigan came into InfoCision Stadium on the eve of Veterans Day and ran the ball right through us for 360 yards. Final score, Western Michigan 42, Akron 14. We're 1-9 and 0-6 in the MAC, and I still showed up early with my flag pin on.

Here's the figure that hurts most: 42:46. That's how long the Broncos held the football. We had it for 17:14. You can't win a game you're watching from the bench. They converted 13 of 17 third downs, and Cole Cabana broke an 82-yard run early in the second quarter that I'm going to see in my sleep.

But this is the Rubber City, and rubber bounces. Cibastian Broughton answered that Cabana run three plays later, hitting Marcel Williams for 35 yards and a touchdown to make it 14-7. In the fourth quarter, same two guys, 39 yards, another score. Williams finished with 5 catches for 85 yards and both touchdowns. Broughton went 12 of 18 for 173 yards. When those two are rolling, Akron has a heartbeat.

Give it up for the defense on fourth down, too. Western Michigan went for it four times and converted once. On the very first drive, Cyrus Durham helped drop Broc Lowry for a 9-yard loss on fourth-and-1, and the Broncos had to hand it back. Tairan Davis Jr. made 15 tackles, 13 of them by himself. That man was everywhere, and he deserved more help.

Brandon Hills took seven kickoffs back for 139 yards, which tells you two facts. He's tough, and we gave up a lot of points. Jordan Gant ran 9 times for 61 yards, and I wanted to see him 20 more times.

Now the honest part. We gave up 566 yards. Jalen Buckley ran for 121 and two scores, Cabana for 107, and their two quarterbacks completed 22 of 24 throws between them. One Bronco drive went 17 plays and ate 9:19 of clock. That's not a bad night. That's a long night.

Next Wednesday, Nov. 18, it's Akron at UMass, 7:00 PM ET at McGuirk. Feed Marcel Williams early, keep our defense off the field, and let's bring one more win home to Summit County. Zip, zip, hooray.

articles.title: Western Michigan vs Akron: 360 Rushing Yards and a 42-14 Night in the Rubber City
articles.byline: Corwin Dahlquist, The Western Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Western Michigan Broncos (7-3) 42, Akron Zips (1-9) 14, Tue., Nov. 10, InfoCision Stadium, Akron. Next: vs Eastern Michigan, Tue., Nov. 17, 7:00 PM ET, Waldo Stadium, Kalamazoo
articles.text:
I brought film to Akron, and the film was right. Western Michigan 42, Akron 14, Tuesday night at InfoCision Stadium, and the Broncos are 7-3 and 5-1 in the MAC. Write that down in pen.

Begin with the clock. We held the ball for 42:46. The Zips had it for 17:14. We converted 13 of 17 third downs and ran it 56 times for 360 yards. Every guy up front gets a game ball, and I'd like the record to show I diagrammed this exact plan in the parking lot.

The first drive scared me. Broc Lowry took a fourth-down sack and a hard hit, and Mason Reynolds came in. Reynolds completed his first career throw, per WMU Athletics, ran 35 yards down to the Akron 4, and then found Nate Levicki in the flat for a 3-yard score. Cool as Kalamazoo in November.

Then Cole Cabana did it again. For the second straight game, WMU Athletics says, he went 82 yards for a touchdown, and this one finished a 98-yard drive in four plays. He ended with 107 yards on nine carries, his second straight 100-yard game.

After Akron answered, we put together the drive that broke them: 17 plays, 75 yards, 9:19 off the clock, finished by Jalen Buckley from a yard out for a 21-7 halftime lead. Buckley added a 35-yarder in the third on fourth-and-1, bouncing it outside and down the right sideline. That's 121 yards and two scores for him.

Lowry came back for the second half and didn't miss. Not once. He went 15 for 15 for 149 yards, and his 20-yard touchdown to Keivin Boone-Nelson II was the first touchdown catch of Boone-Nelson's career. Reynolds finished 7 of 8 with two scores, both to Levicki. Baylin Brooks caught a career-high 8 balls for 78 yards.
